sections.h2: Which McKee offices touch a Jackson County tax bill?
sections.html:
Property tax in this rural county runs through three McKee offices. One values the land, one collects the money and one keeps the deed books, and the county's officials page lists them all.

  • PVA: P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7634, fax (606) 287-7079. Its listed role is keeping property records and assessing property.
  • Sheriff: P.O. Box 426, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7121. Collecting taxes heads the duties the county lists.
  • County Clerk: P.O. Box 339, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7800. Land records, meaning deeds and mortgages, plus transfers, are filed here.

The county site gives phone numbers and not a payment portal, so call the Sheriff to learn which payment methods and counter hours apply.

sections.h2: What dates matter for a Jackson County bill?
sections.html:
No local calendar overrides the statewide one. Under KRS 134.015 the bill is due by December 31, and paying everything by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount.

The regular Kentucky collection stages that Jackson County follows (source: KRS 134.015)
When paidResult
By November 12 percent off
November 2 through December 31Printed amount
January5 percent added
February onward10 percent added

A late mailing can lead Revenue to set an alternative schedule with a month per stage. The Sheriff's collecting ends April 15, after which the Clerk holds whatever is unpaid. If your bill never arrives, phone the Sheriff, because a lost bill does not cancel a penalty.

sections.h2: How can a Jackson County owner dispute a value?
sections.html:
The first move is a conference with the PVA. KRS 133.120 treats it as a required first step, scheduled before or during the inspection period, and a telephone conference is available on request.

Still unsatisfied afterward? Mail or deliver a written petition to the County Clerk, naming your reasons and the parcel and stating what you think fair cash value is. It must arrive one workday after the inspection period closes. Rural owners should plan ahead, since the bill itself comes too late to contest.

A public hearing before the board of assessment appeals comes next. Collect the following beforehand:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Loan or mortgage papers on the parcel.

A petition without supporting facts can be denied. During the case, tax stays payable on your claimed value.

sections.h2: How much of a Jackson County house does the homestead exemption cover?
sections.html:
Nearly half. The $49,100 deduction for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, set against the Census middle home value of $111,500, leaves $62,400 to tax. That trims the base by about 44 percent.

Applicants need to be 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program, and live in the house. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport shown at the PVA proves age. Disability claims renew yearly, with exceptions for veterans with service-connected disabilities and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

The deduction attaches to the owner's own residence. After moving, a seller should tell the PVA and file again for the new address.

sections.h2: Who pays when a Jackson County parcel sells with tax unpaid?
sections.html:
The seller should plan to settle it from proceeds. The tax is a personal debt dating from the assessment date, the lien on the land can last 11 years, and at the April 15 cutoff the Clerk files the bill as a certificate of delinquency.

Revenue's explainer gives the timeline. A County Attorney notice goes out within 30 days of transfer, with a second within 60 if needed. KRS 134.128 sets the tax sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the Clerk advertises the list 30 to 45 days before it.

Revenue's worked example shows the price of waiting: a $1,000 bill becomes a $1,254 certificate at transfer and costs $1,659.90 if paid after the June advertisement. Those totals assume a commission, so ask the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for the real number.

sections.h2: Where does a Jackson County deed get recorded, and what tax applies?
sections.html:
The County Clerk in McKee handles it. The same office issues vehicle and marriage licenses, keeps wills and notary bonds, and gathers the state transfer tax before taking a deed.

KRS 142.050 bills the grantor 50 cents per $500 of value. At $111,500, the Census middle value, the count is exactly 223 units, so the tax is $111.50. Gifts with nominal value, divorcing spouses and foreclosure transfers are among the exempt cases.

Ask the Clerk for the current recording fee before closing, since the statute sets that amount and lawmakers can change it.

sections.h2: What do household numbers say about Jackson County housing?
sections.html:
Jackson County's middle home value of $111,500 is less than half of Jefferson County's $248,400. The county counted 5,122 households in 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.53 people each, and 91.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

  • Monthly owner costs: $1,101 with a mortgage and $355 without.
  • Poverty rate: 22.0 percent.
  • Adults 25 or older with a high school diploma: 75.1 percent, and with a bachelor's degree: 8.8 percent.
  • Households with a broadband subscription: 83.1 percent.
  • Veterans: 583.
  • Building permits in 2025: zero.

The Census recorded zero building permits for 2025, so new construction added no supply that year. Sellers here are almost always dealing with an existing house, and the assessment on it traces back to the PVA's January 1 value.

sections.h2: What is the Jackson County landscape like for a seller?
sections.html:
Jackson County sits where the Cumberland Plateau meets the Bluegrass, with ground from about 600 to 1,600 feet above sea level. It was formed in 1858 from parts of Madison, Estill, Owsley, Clay, Laurel and Rockcastle counties. McKee is the seat, and Annville is the largest community.

Karst ground in the north produces caves such as Wind Cave near the Turkey Foot campground, and the Middle Fork of the Rockcastle River rises in the south. Some 56,000 acres, about a quarter of the county, belong to the Daniel Boone National Forest, and the Sheltowee Trace trail has a trailhead in McKee. US 421 runs north toward Berea and Richmond and south toward Manchester. KY 30 links the county to I-75 and the Mountain Parkway. There is no hospital in the county, so residents drive to Berea, Richmond, London or Manchester.

  • 13,325 people lived here in 2025, a 2.8 percent gain on 2020.
  • 345.2 square miles of land, with 37.5 people per square mile.
  • Owners occupy 77.4 percent of homes.
  • $665 median gross rent and $40,000 median household income.
  • A mean commute of 37.7 minutes.

Three industrial parks, in Annville, McKee and Sandgap, anchor local jobs, and the Jackson County Fair and Homecoming runs the weekend before Labor Day. Jackson Energy supplies power, and the Jackson County Water Association serves homes outside McKee.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Jackson County PVA?
faqs.a: Write to P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, or call (606) 287-7634. Fax goes to (606) 287-7079.

faqs.q: What is the discount for paying early?
faqs.a: Two percent off, provided the full bill is paid by November 1 as KRS 134.015 allows. Afterward the amount on the bill applies until the year ends.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost?
faqs.a: The statute adds 5 percent during January and 10 percent after that. A bill unpaid at the April 15 cutoff moves to the Clerk, where monthly interest of 1 percent and commissions begin.

faqs.q: Can a seller keep the homestead exemption after leaving?
faqs.a: No. The exemption covers the home the owner lives in, so after closing the seller tells the PVA and files again for the new residence.

faqs.q: Is the deed recorded at the McKee courthouse?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Clerk there files deeds and mortgages and collects the transfer tax of 50 cents per $500. Phone (606) 287-7800 to confirm current fees.
